Inputs read: card #12464 (body, triage `6190403616`, claim `6190903933`, dev report `6191722258`), the split-off card #12486 (body), PR #12485 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at the merge base `d9d9d9868`), the 37 check-runs on this head (34 success, 3 skipped; `Spec Main Shape Gate`, `Type Check`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Claim Re-read` and `Changeset Bump Policy` all success), the spec's `PageSchema.kind` at objectstack `c5dd7fce30` (`packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts`, read from the objectstack checkout) and in the published `@objectstack/spec@18.0.0-next.1` tarball (`dist/ui/index.mjs`, which objectui's lockfile resolves for every workspace package).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The TS face narrows to `'full' | 'slotted' | 'html' | 'react'` — right, and it extends the spec `Page` at both ends.** At `c5dd7fce30` the spec's `kind` is `enumWithRetiredValues(['full', 'slotted', 'html', 'react'], PAGE_KIND_RETIRED_GUIDANCE).default('full')`, and `enumWithRetiredValues` returns a plain `z.enum(values, { error })`, so the spec's own union is exactly these four. The published `18.0.0-next.1` (built 2026-10-14T12:08Z, before the retirement merged at 09:48Z the next day; `gitHead` absent) still declares `kind: z.enum(["full", "slotted", "html", "react", "jsx"]).default("full")` and `COMPILED_PAGE_KINDS = ["html", "jsx"]`. A four-member union is a subtype of both, so `PageNodeSchema extends Omit<SpecPage, PAGE_SPEC_EXCLUDED | 'slots'>` holds against `next.1` (the `Type Check` run on this head) and against spec `main` (the `Spec Main Shape Gate` run on this head, which force-runs `pnpm type-check --continue` repo-wide against a spec built from objectstack `main`; the objectstack `main` head at the run's time, `8044f4d5` at 11:57Z, descends from `c5dd7fce30`, and `page.zod.ts` has not changed since). The triage's TS2430 red on `main` is therefore closed by this diff. The new pin `page-kind-jsx-retired-12464.test.ts` asserts `Equal` on the whole union and carries a `@ts-expect-error` on `kind: 'jsx'`; `packages/types`' `type-check` script runs `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the directive is in a compiled program, not a phantom check.

2. **The zod face (`packages/types/src/zod/layout.zod.ts`, outside the claim's surface): `kind: stripImportedDefaults(SpecPageSchema).shape.kind.unwrap().extract([...four...]).optional()` — right mechanism.** On both spec versions `kind` is a `ZodDefault` over a `ZodEnum`; `stripImportedDefaults` turns the default into an optional, `.unwrap()` yields the enum, and `.extract` picks members by reference. On spec `main` the four are the whole enum (identity); on `next.1` the pick drops `jsx`, so `safeParse({ kind: 'jsx' })` fails at path `kind` (the vitest pin); and `.extract` is typed over the enum's own keys, so a spec that drops a kind fails this file's compile instead of silently diverging. It is the same shape as the existing `PAGE_KIND_NODE_TYPE = PageTypeSchema.extract([...])` in the same file. A `WiderThanDeclared` ledger entry would have been the alternative, and the dev is right that it cannot be correct on both spec versions at once. **Runtime readers, verified:** the only non-test import of a page-carrying zod schema from `@object-ui/types/zod` is `packages/cli/src/utils/authoring-face.ts` (`StrictAnyComponentSchema.safeParse`, behind `objectui validate` / `objectui check`); the other three runtime importers (`plugin-dashboard/measureRefusal.ts`, `plugin-designer/DashboardEditor.tsx`, `plugin-map/ObjectMap.tsx`) parse dashboard-widget and map configs, not pages. The render path does not touch it: `SchemaRenderer` calls `@object-ui/core`'s hand-written structural `validateSchema` (`core/src/validation/schema-validator.ts` imports no zod schema), and `app-shell`'s `MetadataService` parses with the spec's own schemas, not objectui's zod face. So a stored `jsx` page served by a `next.1` server is not refused anywhere on the render path; it still reaches the renderer's `'jsx'` arm. No FAIL here. One observation, not a defect: on `next.1` the objectui-side refusal carries zod's anonymous enum message (no `html` prescription), since `next.1` ships no retired-value guidance; once the resolved spec carries `c5dd7fce30`, the spec's own prescription rides through `.extract`.

3. **`page.tsx`: `const kind: string | undefined = schema.kind` — right per triage's half-2 deferral.** Narrowing the type made `kind === 'jsx'` a TS2367 in the components declaration build, so half 1 could not leave the file untouched. The widening annotation (no cast, no `as`) keeps every existing arm compiling and changes nothing at runtime: the `'react'`, `'html' || 'jsx'` and template branches are byte-for-byte the same comparisons. No `jsx` to `html` mapping was added. The comment states the pin window honestly. The arm's removal stays with #12486, as triage prescribed.

4. **Authoring and doc surfaces now present `html` only — right, with the leftovers accounted for.** At this head, `kind: 'jsx'` is authored nowhere in `apps/`, `packages/*/src` (non-test), `content/docs`, `skills` or `docs`; `react-pages.md` and the `layout.ts` docblock now say the alias was retired and to author `html`; the console sample and its extraction pin read `html`. What still names `jsx` as current: the `getJsxManifest` comment in `page.tsx`, the re-attached-checks comment in `layout.zod.ts` (which describes `next.1`'s `COMPILED_PAGE_KINDS`, so it is literally true today), and the app-shell server double in `ResourceEditPage.pageRequiresStamp-11357.test.tsx` (test-only, mirrors `next.1`). All three are named in the dev report and carried by #12486 (its items 2 and 3). The sample's file name `sdui-jsx-preview.*` names the parse tier, carries no kind value, and is correctly left alone.

### ② Semver level

- **`@object-ui/types: minor` — matches the diff and the `Clause-②: yes` line.** The published `PageNodeSchema.kind` narrows (a literal typed `kind: 'jsx'` stops compiling; the zod face refuses it), which is breaking, and objectui levels a breaking change `minor` (fixed group, `major` reserved for the cross-major sync with `@objectstack`; `check-changeset-no-major` passed). The changeset body spells out the breaking semantics and the `html` replacement, as the policy asks.
- **`@object-ui/console: patch` — right.** The console is published (no `private`), its sample page's `kind` changed, and nothing about its contract moved.
- **`@object-ui/components` omitted — acceptable.** The presence rule (AGENTS.md and `check-changeset-presence.mjs`) asks that a PR touching a fixed-group package's `src/` carry a changeset declaration; it does not demand one entry per touched package, and `Changeset Declaration` passed on this head. In the fixed group `@object-ui/components` is versioned together with `types` regardless, so no bump is lost; the only effect is that its CHANGELOG carries no line for a type-annotation-only edit with unchanged behaviour, and the `types` changeset already records that the renderer is unchanged. Half 2's own `@object-ui/components: minor` is correctly reserved for #12486, where behaviour does change.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Out-of-surface edit, `packages/types/src/zod/layout.zod.ts` — answered.** The claim's surface was derived from the card's premise that the zod directory carries no `jsx` kind; that was measured on literal text, and the zod `PageNodeSchema` inherited `kind` from the spec by reference. With the TS face narrowed, `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` turned the package's own type-check red (two TS2322), so half 1 was not shippable without this file. The edit is the same narrowing's zod half, follows an in-file precedent, and the dev declared it in the report with the alternative (a ledger entry) and why it was rejected. I accept the in-place exemption; the PM should add the file to the claim surface on record. Escalation: none needed beyond that bookkeeping.
- **`page.tsx` edited in half 1 — answered.** Forced by TS2367; the edit is a widening annotation and a comment, no behaviour, and the half-2 deliverable (dropping the arm) is untouched. Within the triage's intent.
- **Half 2 deferred to #12486 — answered.** The pin reading is correct (`next.1` is older than the retirement commit; `npm view @objectstack/spec@next` is `18.0.0-next.1`). #12486 carries the `Restart-when:` line verbatim from triage, is `pm:on-hold` and marked not-a-claim, and its steps 1 to 5 cover restoring the `kind` read, the two stale comments, the app-shell test double, a non-compilation pin, and the `components` changeset. All three of the dev's noted leftovers are on it.
- **Model-free commit trailers — not a deviation.** The three commits end with `Claude-Session:` plus `Co-authored-by: Claude` with no model identifier, which is the pair AGENTS.md prescribes; the harness's model-named reminder is the lower-precedence instruction. Nothing to escalate.
